parts.text: Cross-project refs ({{ ref() }}) work across dbt projects on Enterprise and Enterprise+ plans, enabling references to models in other projects to support multi-project deployments. "Cross-project references ... is the foundational feature that enables the multi-project deployments. `{{ ref() }}`s now work across dbt projects"
dbt Catalog provides full, cross-project lineage to discover dependencies across multiple projects. "Catalog ... complete with full, cross-project lineage."

Groups let you organize DAG nodes by logical area and assign an owner to the entire group for governance. "With groups, you can organize nodes in your dbt DAG that share a logical connection ... and assign an owner to the entire group."
Access configs allow you to control who can reference models, enforcing cross-project reference permissions. "Access configs allow you to control who can reference models."

Model Versions provide versioning so teams can treat models as stable APIs for cross-project adoption and deprecation. "Model versioning is the mechanism to allow graceful adoption and deprecation of models as they evolve."

Model Contracts let you set explicit expectations on data shape to prevent upstream changes breaking downstream consumers. "Model Contracts  data contracts set explicit expectations on the shape of the data to ensure data changes upstream ... don't break downstream consumers' data products."

Cross-project refs resolve to Production by default; if a project defines both Production and Staging, refs from development and Staging environments resolve to Staging while refs from Production resolve to Production. By default, cross-project references resolve to the "Production" deployment environment... If a project defines both a "Production" environment and a "Staging" environment, then cross-project references from development and "Staging" environments will resolve to "Staging," whereas only references coming from "Production" environments will resolve to "Production."

Contracts can only be applied at the model level and apply to the entire model, including all output columns; you cannot apply contracts to sources or to part of a model. No, contracts can only be applied at the model level. No. A contract applies to an entire model, including all columns in the model’s output.

Protected is the default access: protected models can be referenced by any model within the same dbt project or when the project is installed as a package. Protected: Models with a protected access modifier can be referenced by any other model within the same dbt project or when the project is installed as a package. This is the default setting for all models...
Private models are referenceable only by models within the same group. Private: A model with a private access modifier is only referenceable by models within the same group.

To deprecate a model (or downgrade its access), mark it with deprecation_date to deliver a warning to all downstream consumers. they should mark that model for deprecation (using deprecation_date), which will deliver a warning to all downstream consumers of that model.
Cross-project references require each project name to be unique in your dbt account. Cross-project references require that each project `name` be unique in your dbt account.

To enable bidirectional project dependencies, each project must run and produce public models before the other can take a dependency on it. Each project must run and produce public models before the original producer project can take a dependency on the original consumer project.

Running `dbt build --select +model` will not run upstream models in other projects unless those upstream projects are installed as packages (source code). No, unless upstream projects are installed as packages (source code). In that case, the models in project installed as a project become "your" models, and you can select or run them.

A dbt Enterprise-tier plan is required to set up multiple projects and reference models across them. Yes, a dbt Enterprise-tier plan is required to set up multiple projects and reference models across them.

Built-in job commands are chained; if one run step fails the entire job fails with an "Error" status. During a job run, built-in commands are "chained" together and if one run step fails, the entire job fails with an "Error" status.
Checkbox steps like 'Generate docs on run' or 'Run source freshness' can fail without failing the whole job if subsequent steps pass. If the step fails, the job can succeed if subsequent steps pass.
By default a deploy job's Commands section includes the dbt build command. By default, it includes the `dbt build` command.

Intervals scheduling runs every N hours from midnight UTC; subsequent runs keep the same offset (e.g., 00:04 -> 02:04 for Every 2 hours). If you choose **Every 2 hours**, the job will run every 2 hours from midnight UTC. ... if the previous scheduled pipeline ran at 00:04 UTC, the next run will be at 02:04 UTC.

dbt job schedules use UTC and do not translate to local time or account for daylight savings. dbt uses Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) and does not account for translations to your specific timezone or take into consideration daylight savings time.

Developer plans enforce a minimum cron scheduling interval of 10 minutes; Starter/Enterprise plans have no execution-frequency restrictions. Developer plans: dbt sets a minimum interval of every 10 minutes for scheduling jobs. ... Starter, Enterprise, and Enterprise+ plans: No restrictions on job execution frequency.

The 'Run when another job finishes' trigger (job chaining) requires a Starter or Enterprise-tier dbt plan. For the [Trigger on job completion] feature, your dbt account must be on the [Starter or an Enterprise-tier] plan.

By default a job inherits the dbt version from its environment; changing the job-level version is discouraged except for upgrades. By default, its set to inherit the dbt version from the environment. dbt Labs strongly recommends that you don't change the default setting.
Job 'Threads' defaults to 4; increasing threads raises model execution concurrency. By default, its set to 4 threads. Increase the thread count to increase model execution concurrency.

Compare changes 'No deferral' is default; options are 'Environment' or 'This Job' and deferral-to-environment compares against the environment's manifest.json. By default, its set to **No deferral**. Select either **Environment** or **This Job**... deferral to an environment is more efficient as dbt will compare against the project representation (which is stored in the `manifest.json`) of the last successful deploy job run that executed in the deferred environment.
